items.t: In Willoughby Heights, houses sold at a median of $1,470,000 across 179 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,315,000 and $1,636,666. The median house sat 26 days and sold for 96.7% of list.
Willoughby Heights: 446 townhomes sold at a median of $830,500, with the middle half between $755,000 and $919,900. The median townhome took 18 days to sell and closed at 98.6% of list.

390 condos sold in Willoughby Heights at a median of $560,000 (middle half $465,000 to $625,000). A typical condo in Willoughby Heights spent 25 days on the market and closed at 97.4% of the asking price.
In Willoughby Heights, duplexes sold at a median of $1,200,000 across 41 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,169,900 and $1,240,000. The median duplex sat 34 days and sold for 96.7% of list.

blocks.text: Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How Willoughby Heights compares with the rest of Langley

items.t: Houses in Willoughby Heights have the 5th highest median of 9 Langley sub-areas, $1,470,000. Aldergrove is lowest at $1,025,000 and Campbell Valley highest at $2,565,000. Brookswood ($1,415,000) sits just below and Murrayville ($1,487,250) sits just above.

Of 6 Langley sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Willoughby Heights ranks second highest at $830,500; the range is $560,000 (Aldergrove) to $1,395,000 (Fort Langley). Walnut Grove ($820,000) sits just below and Fort Langley ($1,395,000) sits just above.

Condos in Willoughby Heights have the second highest median of 7 Langley sub-areas, $560,000. Aldergrove is lowest at $432,500 and Fort Langley highest at $800,000. Murrayville ($542,500) sits just below and Fort Langley ($800,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, duplexes are the newest homes selling in Willoughby Heights (median 2025) and houses the oldest (median 2011), a gap of 14 years.
